title: Audit runner for quant calibration and accuracy gates
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Goal: Build a resilient, automated audit runner that validates quantization profiles (FP8 and INT8) against a reproducible reference prompt set and enforces pass/fail gates for model promotion. The runner must be deterministic for regression repros, integrate with CI, and report structured metrics to Console so PM/RE can quickly interpret regressions.

Scope:
- Accepts a QProfile (calibration parameters + per-layer scale tables) and a model binary.
- Runs a configurable set of reference prompts (seeded reference set + adversarial variants) across temperature and sampling modes.
- Computes a multi-signal accuracy fingerprint: answer equivalence delta, token-level KL/logprob shift, embedding cosine drift, ROUGE/L, and a blackbox regression score (ensemble of heuristics).
- Applies per-metric thresholds and a composite pass/fail gate that can be tuned per-model and per-release.
- Saves deterministic artifacts (outputs, RNG seeds, KV warmup traces) for forensic replay.
- Ships telemetry events for failure classes and aggregates histograms for Console dashboards.

Architecture/Implementation notes:
- Orchestrator: lightweight Python runner that spins multiple trials in parallel using the same serving runtime harness. Use existing job queue (k8s CronJob prototype) for scheduling; early runs will use a dedicated GPU node pool.
- Replay engine: record requests and seeds for exact replay; store artifacts in s3 path: s3://redwood-audit/ENG-61234/{model}/{qprofile}/{run_id}.
- Determinism: pin RNG, disable sampling where required, and provide a deterministic decode mode matching the runtime's kernel ordering.
- Warmup harness: emulate production KV cache priming to capture cache-dependent regressions for long-context flows.
- Failure classification: tag failures as 'semantic divergence', 'token-delta', 'timeout', 'nan/overflow', or 'infrastructure' to drive correct next actions.

Metrics and Gates: initial gate config (pilot):
- Answer equivalence (exact/top-1 match on normalized tokens) >= 98% or composite semantic passthrough >= 95%.
- Embedding cosine >= 0.995 (for high-sensitivity litmus prompts).
- Token-level average logprob delta <= 0.12 nats/token.
- Outlier rate (large hallucinations / leading-to-wrong-facts) <= 0.5%.
- Overall composite score must exceed threshold; failing a single high-confidence prompt can mark the run as FAIL.

Integrations and automation:
- CI: a GitHub Action job (pr/audit-run) that triggers when a QProfile is updated or a model promotion PR is opened. A successful audit is required to enable the rollout pipeline.
- Console: surface per-run dashboards and weekly regression emails. Wire Alerting to PagerDuty if a promoted profile causes a regression for existing customers.
- GitHub: link PRs from model onboarding to the audit run artifacts. Example PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4812 (pilot runner), https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/183 (qprofile changes).
- Confluence: design doc and gate philosophy: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/92345/Quant+Audit+Runner

Pilot plan and rollout:
Phase 1 (pilot, 2 weeks): wire runner to 3 canonical models (open-13B, open-7B, small-3B) and an initial reference prompt set of ~2k prompts drawn from product evals + internal golden-like seeds. Validate determinism and storage of artifacts.
Phase 2 (ci gating, 3 weeks): integrate with PR checks and add dashboarding + regression emails.
Phase 3 (scale, 4 weeks): expand to multiple model families, build per-model threshold configs, add adversarial generation and automatic rerun heuristics.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Running full reference suite per QProfile is expensive; we'll gate heavy runs to reserved capacity and implement a cheap smoke check (200 prompts) for fast PR feedback.
- Strict gates may block useful low-cost quant profiles; we'll provide a canary label that allows warning-only results for non-production channels.
- Determinism across runtime kernel changes is non-trivial; we will decouple determinism validation from the accuracy gate by running a dedicated determinism-only job when runtime upgrades land.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end audit runner that completes pilot runs for 3 models and stores artifacts reproducibly.
- CI check that fails PRs when the composite gate is not met.
- Console dashboard showing per-metric deltas and run history.
- Post-mortem runbook for debugging failures and replaying artifacts.

Next steps (short-term):
- (Miguel) land pilot orchestrator PR and create s3 buckets + IAM roles.
- (Aisha) finalize reference prompt selection and thresholds; produce confluence doc draft for review.
- (Evelyn - QA) author smoke-test set and validate runner determinism on dev infra.
